contexts.text: In this and the following chapters (, 41) the behemoth and the leviathan are treated of, and the natural man is signified by both of them; by the behemoth, the natural man as to the goods which are called the delights of natural love; and by the leviathan, the natural man as to the truths which are called scientifics and Knowledges, from which comes natural lumen.
By the behemoth () is meant the same as by a beast, namely, the natural affections which are in man; wherefore it is said, Behold the behemoth which I have made with thee.
